title: Ensure pam_unix does not include nullok
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 5.3.3.4.1: Ensure pam_unix does not include nullok

fields.description: Raw PAM configuration lines that were checked

steps.name: Check if PAM configuration files exist
steps.function: 1. Check if PAM configuration files exist using command: `ls /etc/pam.d/password-auth /etc/pam.d/system-auth`. Expected result: Both files exist.

steps.name: Check that pam_unix.so lines do not include nullok
steps.function: 2. Check that pam_unix.so lines do not include nullok using command: `grep -P -- '^\h*(auth|account|password|session)\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_unix\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/password-auth /etc/pam.d/system-auth`. Expected result: None of the returned lines includes 'nullok'.

steps.name: Check overall compliance status
steps.function: 3. Check overall compliance status. Expected result: PASS if all checks pass, SKIP if PAM configuration files do not exist, FAIL if pam_unix.so lines include nullok.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
reference_procedure:
Run the following command to verify that the nullok argument is not set on the pam_unix.so module:
# grep -P --
'^\h*(auth|account|password|session)\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_ unix\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/{password,system}-auth
Verify that none of the returned lines includes nullok. Output should be similar to:
/etc/pam.d/password-auth:auth   sufficient   pam_unix.so
/etc/pam.d/password-auth:account   required   pam_unix.so
/etc/pam.d/password-auth:password   sufficient   pam_unix.so sha512 shadow use_authtok
/etc/pam.d/password-auth:session   required   pam_unix.so

/etc/pam.d/system-auth:auth   sufficient   pam_unix.so
/etc/pam.d/system-auth:account   required   pam_unix.so
/etc/pam.d/system-auth:password   sufficient   pam_unix.so sha512 shadow use_authtok
/etc/pam.d/system-auth:session   required   pam_unix.so
